title: Surge Mitigator: soft-state cooperative throttling and graceful limiter fallback
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: During sudden regional traffic surges and intermittent limiter outages we observe unfair token admission, cascading tail latency, and poor SLO adherence for high-priority customers. Existing limiter is single-region authoritative; when it degrades requests either pile up or are hard-shed without graceful degradation. Goal: introduce a Surge Mitigator that (1) enables soft-state cooperative throttling across regions, (2) provides a deterministic graceful-fallback mode for limiter outages, and (3) preserves per-customer fairness while minimizing SLO impact and cost.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New cooperative throttling protocol implemented in admission proxy and regional limiter that exchanges compact soft-state credits; 2) On limiter outage, proxy uses fallback admission (local permissive budget + Retry-After semantics) and circuit-breaker states to avoid cascading failures; 3) Fairness algorithm (decaying credits + per-client smoothing window) demonstrated in load tests with <=10% extra error budget burn for low-priority customers and <2% for P0 customers; 4) Dashboards for new metrics and alerts shipping and validated; 5) Canary rollout completes with automatic rollback on SLO regressions
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed - protocol design doc drafted (confluence: /RegionalResilience/SurgeMitigator); compared approaches: central token service vs soft-state peer exchange; chose soft-state to avoid central single point and cross-region latency.

2026-02-25: Prototype implemented in admission-proxy with local token-bucket smoothing and a compact credit-exchange message over control plane (protobuf v2). Initial bench shows 15% CPU overhead under steady-state, but 40% improvement in tail latency during synthetic surges.
2026-03-02: Design review (eng + product) - agreed to prioritize P0 customer preservation and opt-in for Dedicated tenants. Decided to keep heuristic thresholds configurable per-region and per-tier.

2026-03-07: Implementation: added circuit-breaker state machine (CLOSED, PROBING, OPEN) in limiter core; on OPEN the proxy consults soft-state cache and applies local permissive budgets with strict Retry-After headers. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/8742

2026-03-11: Load test 1 (in-region surge): fairness algorithm reduces head-of-line blocking for mixed-priority traffic; observed 1.7% extra error budget for P0 traffic (target <2%). Adjusted decay half-life from 30s->18s for faster recovery.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for credit-exchange serialization and state transitions; 2) Integration tests with two-region simulator: simulate limiter outage in region-A while region-B receives surge; measure request success, latency, and Retry-After behavior; 3) Chaos: kill limiter process and network partition during canary; 4) Synthetic customer-mix workloads (P0/P1/P2) at 5x baseline for 15 minutes; 5) Run long-duration soak for 12 hours to verify steady-state CPU/memory impact
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): enable feature-flag in staging for all regions; Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of traffic in us-east and eu-west for Dedicated + Hosted non-enterprise, monitor 48h SLOs; Phase 2 (ramped): 25% -> 75% over 1 week with automated rollback on SLO regression or increased 5xx rate; Phase 3: full rollout and mark GA. Provide opt-out knob for enterprise tenants until policy acceptance.
metrics: Metrics to add: limiter.credit_exchanges_per_min, limiter.local_permissive_budget_used, limiter.circuit_state{region}, admissions.success_rate{priority,region}, admissions.retries_after_header_pct, slo.error_budget_burn_rate{customer_tier}. Alerts: P0_admission_rate_drop > 1% for 5m, error_budget_burn_rate > 0.05 for 10m, circuit_state OPEN count > 1 for 2m
